summary:
Delaware is a state within the United States, so entry rules, passport and visa policy, and federal identity screening are governed entirely by federal measures rather than Delaware law. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary; the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, new passport applications are decided as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already issued with an X marker remain valid until expiry. Trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at application, with some left stranded abroad; the ACLU is litigating on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and in November 2025 the Supreme Court allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992.

Visa screening carries its own exposure: since 25 February 2025 the State Department flags visa applicants with an internal marking and treats listing a gender other than the one assigned at birth as fraud carrying a permanent bar, and the Transportation Security Administration's checkpoint procedures involve secondary screening, hand-held devices and pat-downs that risk outing a trans traveller.

Delaware itself imposes no ban on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity, per the Movement Advancement Project equality map. A July 2026 national legal risk assessment places Delaware in its Low-Risk States group (AZ, DE, ME, MI, NV, PA, VA, WI, DC), describing states that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection.

Delaware law has prohibited discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas since SB 97, signed 19 June 2013 and effective immediately. Since 2013 Delaware imposes additional penalties for a violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived gender identity. Since March 26, 2016 Delaware has prohibited discrimination based on gender identity within insurance contracts, including sex reassignment surgery. An 11 August 2009 executive order protects state executive-branch employees from gender-identity discrimination.

Delaware SB 65, signed and effective 23 July 2018, defines conversion therapy to include practices seeking to change gender identity, behaviours or gender expressions and makes it unprofessional conduct subject to discipline for physicians, nurses, mental health and chemical dependency professionals, psychologists and clinical social workers to perform on a minor or refer a minor out of state for.

Transgender people may change their legal gender on state-issued identification with only the signed statement of a licensed medical provider. As of 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery is no longer an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate, which instead requires a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. A 2015 law, signed 25 June 2015 and effective immediately, allows inmates to access and change the name on birth certificates to reflect gender identity. As of April 2020 Delaware does not offer a gender X marker on drivers' licences.

In January 2025 Governor Hall-Long signed an executive order creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission. HB142, to formally repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defence and ban its usage, was introduced in May 2023 and passed both houses of the Legislature in June 2023, with the Governor yet to sign or veto it.

Prisoner housing policy is federal and has shifted repeatedly: a January 2015 ICE memo directed housing transgender immigration detainees according to gender identity, and 2016 Department of Justice guidelines forbade corrections agencies from assigning trans inmates to men's or women's units solely on birth anatomy; in 2018 the Federal Bureau of Prisons revised its Transgender Offender Manual in the opposite direction, making placement a case-by-case basis in which biological sex is the initial determination and gender identity is used only in rare cases. No Delaware-specific placement policy is documented.
tangentialFactors:
Delaware's low-risk standing sits within a national pattern moving the other way: state bathroom bans applying to trans people cover 9 states and 1 territory, gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states, and in March 2026 Kansas enacted a law invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not match sex assigned at birth, which rights groups describe as a template for other state legislatures. Delaware has enacted none of these measures.

The federal layer applies uniformly regardless of state posture. Executive Order 14187 of 28 January 2025 described gender-affirming care for minors as mutilation; in summer 2025 the Department of Justice subpoenaed more than 11 hospitals for full records of patients under 19; and in October 2025 proposed health-department rules would bar Medicaid reimbursement for care to transgender patients under 18. Several federal orders have been blocked or enjoined in court, so the operative position on any given measure should be checked before travel.

Official hostility at federal level includes a December 2025 instruction that the FBI offer cash bounties for information leading to the identification and arrest of transgender activists described as promoting radical gender ideology, and a May 2026 national counterterrorism strategy prioritising the identification and neutralisation of groups whose ideology is described as anti-American, radically pro-transgender and anarchist.
localsOnly:
Since 2013 Delaware law prohibits discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas under SB 97, which passed the Senate 11-7 on 6 June 2013, passed the House 24-17 with amendments, passed the Senate on amendments 11-9 on 18 June, was signed the next day and took effect immediately. Since 2013 Delaware imposes additional penalties for committing a violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived gender identity.

Since March 26, 2016 Delaware has prohibited discrimination based on gender identity within insurance contracts, including sex reassignment surgery. An executive order of 11 August 2009 protects employees of state executive-branch departments and agencies from discrimination on the basis of gender identity and reauthorized the Governor's Council on Equal Employment Opportunity with a charge to foster an inclusive environment among executive-branch employees.

Delaware SB 65, introduced 26 April 2017 and signed and effective 23 July 2018 as Laws of Delaware 81:340, defines conversion therapy to include practices seeking to change gender identity, behaviors or gender expressions and makes it unprofessional conduct subject to discipline for physicians, nurses, mental health and chemical dependency professionals, psychologists and clinical social workers to perform it on a minor or refer a minor out-of-state for it, while prohibiting the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families from performing or recommending it for a minor.

Transgender people are allowed to change their legal gender requiring only the signed statement of a licensed medical provider for the marker on state-issued identification. As of 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery is no longer an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate, requiring instead a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. A 2015 law signed 25 June 2015 and effective immediately allows inmates to access and/or change the name on birth certificates to reflect gender identity, where previously inmates could only change names due to religious beliefs. As of April 2020 Delaware does not have gender X available on drivers' licenses.

In January 2025 Governor Hall-Long signed an Executive Order creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission. HB142 to formally repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defense and ban its usage was introduced in May 2023, passed both houses of the Legislature in June 2023, with the Governor yet to either sign or veto.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1 January 1973 following repeal of the sodomy law in July 1972. Since 2009 Delaware law has prohibited discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived sexual orientation, supplemented by the August 2009 executive order for state executive branch employees. Since 2001 Delaware has imposed additional penalties for violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived sexual orientation. Civil unions were available 1 January 2012, and same-sex marriage was legalized effective 1 July 2013 with conversion of civil unions to marriages. SB 65 banning conversion therapy on minors passed the Senate 12-3 on 17 May 2017 and the House 24-14 on 7 June 2018, was signed in July 2018 and went into effect immediately. In June 2021 a law was implemented to protect individuals from discrimination based on HIV medicine and PrEP, and in April 2017 the Legislature passed a law allowing HIV patients to donate to other HIV patients, signed and effective 1 January 2018.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project equality map URL cited for Delaware's absence of a facilities ban returned HTTP 404 at the archived address; the finding of no such ban for Delaware is taken from the underlying map's tracking and is not independently re-verified in this pass.

No Delaware-specific policy governing the placement of transgender inmates in state custody is documented in the available sources; the placement history cited is federal (ICE and the Federal Bureau of Prisons) and its current operative text after the 2018 revision is not confirmed here.

HB142's final status is unresolved: it passed both legislative houses in June 2023, but no source records a signature or veto, so whether the gay and trans panic defence remains available in Delaware is not settled in this inventory.

Delaware's current driver's licence gender-marker options are stated as of April 2020; whether a third marker or an updated process has been introduced since is not sourced.
